metadata.name: COL4
metadata.copyrightInfo: © 2026 RJGreenCFI. Based on the Columbia 400 (LC41-550FG) POH/AFM RC050005 Rev. G (16 Oct 07) with Garmin G1000 and GFC 700. Not a substitute for the POH.

items.prompt: Above 12,000 ft PA per 1,000 ft: VO -3, VFE -2.4, VNO -3.5, VNE -4.4 kt. PFD corrects, backup ASI does not.
Usable fuel depends on S/N: 98 gal (41501-41799), 86 gal (41800 on), 102 gal long range (POH Section 2).
Pitot tube gets hot within one minute. Limit the ground test to one or two minutes.
All leading edge devices (stall strips and tapes) must be installed and in good condition for flight (POH 2-13).
No oil pressure in 30 seconds: shut down and investigate.
No start in 30 sec: release starter, cool 3 to 5 min. Never engage while the prop turns.
Vapor suppression may stay on through the start, off a minute after. Moderately warm: a few seconds of prime.
SpeedBrakes slightly extended after the test indicate a failure: pull the SpeedBrake circuit breaker.
Any autotrim test failure: do not use the autopilot until the fault is corrected.
GFC 700 preflight test: white PFT clears in 2 to 3 seconds. A red PFT means no autopilot or flight director (POH 2-11).
A/C on the ground: keep 1000 RPM or more and watch ammeters for battery discharge.
Free castering nose wheel: steer with differential braking, as little as possible. Never taxi with the doors fully up.
No RPM drop on a magneto may mean a hot mag. Correct before further operation.
Plug fouling: hold brakes, 2200 RPM, lean to peak RPM 10 sec, full rich, 1700, recheck mags.
Speeds vary with weight (POH Figure 5-11). A rolling start is preferred if the runway allows.
Do not lean in the climb. Max performance climb: 2600 RPM, full throttle, full rich, 110 KIAS.
Vapor suppression ON if TIT rises above 1460°F at full power and full rich, at any altitude (POH Section 2).
Above 65% power rich of peak only. Below 65% up to 50°F lean of peak TIT. Full rich above 85% power.
Above 18,000 ft never pull the throttle to idle without leaning: the engine floods and quits.
Power up: mixture, prop, then throttle. Power down: throttle, prop, then mixture. Watch TIT 1750°F.
Expedited: 2400 RPM, about 25 in, SpeedBrakes up, 165 KIAS. Keep CHT above 240°F.
In long descents clear the engine with partial power now and then: a quit engine may give no indication.
Coupled ILS: CDI auto switching to manual; reselect APR after NAV source change. AP off by 200 ft AGL (POH 2-11).
Avoid 1800 to 1850 RPM on ILS approaches: it can disturb glideslope reception (POH 4-27).
Avoid sideslips with full flaps: the airplane may pitch down. Slips change indicated airspeed up to 5 kt.
Checklist approach speeds: flaps up 95-100, 12° 90-95, 40° 85-90 KIAS (POH Section 4).
Minimum approach speed varies with weight (POH Figure 5-35).
Taxi time counts toward the five minute turbocharger cooldown (POH Section 4).
The regulator trips the alternator above 31.0 V and the PFD shows the alternator out.
Left bus: aileron trim, pitot heat, SpeedBrakes, position and landing lights, fan, A/C.
Right bus: strobes, taxi light, door seal, CO detector, oxygen, display keypad.
Power back while holding the primer confirms partial pump failure. Backup pump engages at 5.5 psi.
Override any pitch or roll change with control force. Do not re-engage until repaired.
Never open a door in flight. Air loads can tear it off the airplane.
Below 400 ft AGL. If the speed cannot be reached, lower the nose and land straight ahead.
If the backup pump is in use, do not go full rich for descent or landing and avoid closing the throttle.
Flaps and trim are electric: keep the masters on until no longer needed. Do not open the doors in flight.
Extinguishant is toxic: ventilate. Use oxygen only once the fire is out.
Partial restore: A/P trim system on, find the bad axis, reset only the good axis breaker.
Recovery may take an extra turn. Pull out reaches 2 to 3 g and up to 160 KIAS.
